newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mixed, key contracts off peaks.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mixed, key contracts off peaks.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mixed in a dull afternoon, down from their session peaks after the dollar turned firm.
September marks, Swiss francs and yen futures all ended higher, but down from their daily highs. Canadian dollars and sterling ended lower.
"They ended mixed, but the dollar was still relatively strong," an IMM currency futures trader said.
Traders said yen futures were the feature early, posting moderate gains after a stronger-than-expected Japanese tankan report slammed dollar/yen to an overnight low of 113.30/20.
The dollar was also capped briefly this morning by weaker-than-expected U.S. May durable goods orders.
May orders fell 0.6 percent, compared with an average forecast for up 0.6 percent. April's orders were revised to up 1.8 percent from up 1.3 percent.
But traders said the reaction to the report was limited, and the dollar drifted up versus the mark and yen in quiet trade the rest of the day.
After the initial strength, September yen futures neither challenged the overnight high of $0.008929 nor the morning's high of $0.008919.
"It was a quiet day all around," another IMM trader said. "There was a little bit of Canada activity, but for the most part it was quiet."
Canadian dollar futures moved steadily lower all morning, but losses were stemmed after the Bank of Canada bought Canadian dollars, traders said.
One trader said the downward drift had begun Tuesday and continued early Wednesday when two firms sold 600 contracts each on the open.
Sterling futures slipped after reaching a new high for the year Tuesday.
Traders said profit-taking after recent gains and a widening UK trade deficit dampened the market.

At the close, September yen was up $0.000076 at $0.008881, marks rose $0.0005 to $0.5836, Swiss francs rose $0.0017 to $0.7028, sterling fell $0.0028 to $1.6596, Canadian dollars fell $0.0018 to $0.7210 and Mexican pesos were $0.000175 lower at $0.121425. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
